subject: computer-science
title: Trees: Binary, BST and AVL
welcome_lead: Search trees and how to keep them balanced.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: binary trees, BST operations, AVL self-balancing.
final_note: Balanced trees keep operations at O(log n).

concepts.def: Each node has up to two children.
Binary search tree — left subtree smaller, right subtree larger.
A self-balancing BST keeping heights within 1.
A local restructure used to rebalance an AVL tree.
Visit left, root, right — yields sorted order on a BST.
Longest path from a node to a leaf.

walkthroughs.body_html: A BST places smaller keys left of each node and larger keys right. Average lookup, insert and delete are O(log n). Inserting sorted data, however, produces a skewed tree with O(n) operations.
AVL trees (Adelson-Velsky and Landis, 1962) re-balance after every insert or delete by performing rotations. Heights of children differ by at most 1, guaranteeing O(log n) operations.
In-order traversal of a BST visits keys in sorted order. Pre-order (root first) and post-order (root last) are used for serialisation and deletion respectively.
